gate_reasoning: Stage 6 scores 22% High, 43% Medium, and 35% Low across 98 claims. The High-confidence core is genuinely strong: IUMI, AAUI, GIA Singapore, PIAM Malaysia, TT Club annual report, IAIS/FSI, AXA XL, Munich Re, Artemis/Vesttoo documentation, and WTW market intelligence collectively anchor the most material claims in this stage (global market sizing, SEA country-level insurance data, Vesttoo fraud evidence, parametric regulatory barriers). The 35% Low rate is driven primarily by two identifiable categories: (1) nine [ASSUMED-N] claims that are correctly self-flagged and properly tagged for field validation — these are structural to the research methodology, not failures; and (2) vendor marketing claims and aggregator market research figures that have not been cross-validated with independent primary sources, concentrated in operating cost estimates (10.2 cents/mile, 1.24% LTL damage rate), adoption statistics (88%/64%/79% telematics figures), and market penetration figures (60-70% SME uninsured). The stage passes the 25% High confidence threshold. It fails the target ≤30% Low threshold (35% Low) primarily due to the ASSUMED tags and vendor-source operating metrics. The flag is warranted because three High-priority weak claims (PP6.1-5 telematics adoption stats, PP6.1-8 SME uninsured baseline, PP6.1-2 operating cost per mile) underpin the core market-sizing and working hypothesis validation for WH5 and WH4 — the two central hypotheses of the research. Deep research on ATRI, NMFTA, ITC, and IUMI sub-data should be targeted at these three before the stage is finalized.
